web_evidence.note: Hachette Book Group's authorized first-four-chapter excerpt consistently narrates Simon externally as he and reports his actions, memories, perceptions, and thoughts in third person.

web_evidence.title: RUN AWAY — Harlan Coben sample

web_evidence.title: 'Run Away,' Please
web_evidence.note: The review explicitly says the plot is told in third person and describes an omniscient narrator plus chapters focalized through Ash and Dee Dee; it treats second-person address as occasional digressive tangents rather than a separate story narration.

person_note: The authorized opening excerpts sustain third-person narration centered on Simon, while the Goodreads passages independently show third-person interior scenes centered on Simon, Elena, Ash, and Dee Dee. The whole-book Crimson review explicitly confirms that the plot is told in third person and characterizes its second-person language as occasional reader-addressing tangents. Generic-you aphorisms, dialogue, prayer, and sign text therefore do not create sustained second-person sections. The main limitation is that the authorized prose sources cover only the opening, but the varied interior quotes and explicit whole-book review resolve that scope limitation without credible contrary evidence.
